- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect downward pressure or mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (true outcome > 70), model frequently overshoots in the following days; cap forecast at +5–10% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in the next 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67); add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment averages > 0.5 over last 7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.33) and price is trending down, model often forecasts a flat or upward path; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5 days to reflect bearish sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (sentiment > 0.67), model tends to lag; add 1–3% to forecast to capture momentum.
